2. Heard Mr. A. Mishra, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. A.K. Mishra, learned Addl.
Government Advocate appearing for the State-opposite parties.

3. The petitioner has filed this writ petition seeking following relief:-
"...... (ii) Issue a writ or order or direction more particularly in the nature of a writ of mandamus directing the opposite party no.1 to 6 cause return of the land acquired under the old Act remains unutilized for a period of five years from the date of taking over the possession, the same shall be returned to the original owner, i.e., petitioner along with his coparceners in interest by reversion thereby awarding compensation to the petitioner as per law keeping in view the failure of the state to protect his land."

4. Mr. A. Mishra, learned counsel for the petitioner contended that since the land has not been utilized and remained unutilized for a period of five years from the date of taking over possession,
the same should be returned to the original owner, the petitioner herein along with his coparceners in interest.
The same having not been done, the petitioner has approached this Court by filing the present writ petition.

5. Mr. A.K. Mishra, learned Addl. Government Advocate appearing for the State-opposite parties contended that the case of the petitioner was considered by the District Magistrate and Collector,
Koraput in Misc. Case No.07/2023 and vide order dated 04.05.2023, the following order was Sadananda Nayak vs State Of Odisha And Others ..... ...

1 passed:-
"Gone through the case record.
The Land Acquisition Officer, Koraput has stated that the abatement was made during the year 1961 and subsequently, the compensation also paid to the recorded tenant.

But the petitioner is claiming that the land acquired under Section 101 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in land acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 that any land acquired under this Act if remains unutilized for a period of five years from the date of taking over the possession, the same shall be returned to the original owner of their heirs.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in land acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is seen that the land was acquired during the year 1961 prior to the commencement of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in land acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 which is not covered under this Act.
Hence the case is rejected on the ground of having no merit.
Pronounced in the open court today, i.e., 4th May 2023."
It is contended that since the petitioner has never challenged the aforesaid order in any forum whatsoever, including this forum, the relief sought in the present writ petition cannot be granted.

Consequentially, dismissal of the writ petition is sought for.
6.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and after going through the records, this Court finds that the Land Acquisition Officer had acquired the land and paid due compensation to the recorded tenant.
The petitioner claimed that the acquired land has not been utilized and, therefore, the same should have been returned to the original owner.
But since the land has been acquired and compensation has been paid, even though the same has not been utilized, question of reversion of the land in favour of the petitioner does not arise.
In any case, nothing has been placed on record to show as to how the land has not been utilized.
More so, since the petitioner has already received the compensation, now he cannot ask for return of the land.
Therefore, this Court is of the considered view that the order dated 04.05.2023 passed by the Collector, Koraput is well justified and does not warrant any interference of this Court.
7. In the above view of the matter, this Court is not inclined to entertain this writ petition, which is accordingly dismissed.
